einzeiler: Former Vanguard CEO Bill McNabb on leadership, indexing, and fintech startups.
kurzfassung: Bill McNabb reflects on his three-decade career at the Vanguard Group, including steering the firm through the 2008 financial crisis. He shares insights on corporate governance from his board seats at IBM and UnitedHealth. Additionally, he discusses his current work advising venture capital firms and fintech startups like Altruist, Vanilla, and Finney.
stichpunkte: Transitioning from teaching Latin and coaching rowing to running the world's largest mutual fund company
The pivotal role of Jack Brennan and Jack Bogle in establishing Vanguard's core values and contrarian indexing philosophy
Navigating the 2008 financial crisis by doubling down on client service and employee job security
Shifting focus to target date funds, ETFs, and the independent advisor channel
Applying long-term strategic thinking from Vanguard to public company boardrooms at IBM and UnitedHealth
Embracing venture capital and advising fintech startups aiming to improve the wealth management ecosystem
The evolution of financial advice, combining advanced technology with the essential human touch

kapitel.titel: From Rowing and Latin to Vanguard
The Rise of Indexing and the 2008 Crisis
The Future of Advice and Closing Thoughts

clips.hook: Index funds beat 90% of active equities over any rolling 10-year period.
clips.text: Over any rolling ten-year timeframe, passive index funds consistently outperform the vast majority of actively managed equities on an after-tax basis.

beschreibung:
Barry speaks with William "Bill" McNabb. He's former chairman and CEO of Vanguard and now sits on the board at UnitedHealth, IBM, Axiom, and Altruist. They discuss his 30+ years at Vanguard and his career after leaving the company, working in the board room and with startups in fintech and more.
